practice_questions.question_text: Explain how cloud infrastructure can let a service run across several geographical regions instead of one local server.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Retains distributed/cloud reasoning as infrastructure purpose and benefit; does not require web-decentralization political claims.
practice_questions.solution: The provider supplies network-accessible computing/storage resources in multiple locations. A service can deploy or replicate workloads across them, so a single local site need not host all processing and capacity can be added where demand occurs.

marking_points.criterion: Explains reduced single-site dependence or capacity benefit.

practice_questions.partial_credit_notes: Award independent criteria up to the stated total; accept equivalent technically correct wording/solutions.

verification.technical: Concrete answer reasoned and checked against full syllabus guidance and available source MS.

practice_questions.question_text: A company can keep all computing on equipment it buys and manages, or rent cloud computing/storage with rapid capacity changes and a provider-managed physical infrastructure. Evaluate the cloud choice for a seasonal service handling confidential records.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Provides infrastructure facts and evaluates purpose/benefits/limits; memorized private/public/hybrid cloud taxonomies are not imposed.
practice_questions.solution: Cloud capacity can expand for seasonal peaks and contract afterwards, avoiding permanent purchase for rare demand. The provider manages physical infrastructure, reducing local maintenance. However, the company depends on connectivity/provider availability and must configure access controls and assess confidentiality obligations. Choose cloud only where those controls and service arrangements meet the records’ needs; elasticity alone does not settle the decision.

marking_points.criterion: Elastic capacity linked to seasonal demand.
